quest.title: The Currents of Life
quest.description: You thought it was all a misunderstanding caused by youkai, not expecting there to be a secret behind it all...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Unknown Item #370519 x1, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, please let me be your partner for the final round of the Test of Courage.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: I'd like your assistance with this investigation, since you two are the only ones who have seen the alleged ghost.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well, that's fine with Paimon. What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Fine by me. Do you have any ideas so far, Heizou?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: I have a few theories, but we don't have enough leads yet.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: There are some places I'd like to investigate first, so you two can accompany me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure! Where would you like to start?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: I want to go back to where we first met up. According to your accounts, you encountered the ghost there and passed out.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: I believe there may still be some clues there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, do we really have to go there? What if we're walking into a trap?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Are you worried that she'll be waiting for us? If anything, that would make things easier.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: My worry is that we won't be able to find her. Honestly, it'd save me a lot of trouble if she were to show up on her own.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow Heizou, you're fearless...

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: The more cases you see, the less afraid you become. Let's go!

talks.objective: Go to the site of the Test of Courage
Go to where you first met the mysterious woman

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: This should be approximately where you first encountered the ghost.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Of course, we cannot conclude whether the woman is actually a ghost or not at this point.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: But I'd like to go over everything that happened again. Do you recall anything she said at the time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, let Paimon think...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She warned us not to go near her, and she said if we didn't leave, our souls would become trapped here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooooh, Paimon doesn't want to remember that moment... Paimon's shivering just thinking about it!

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: And then what happened?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then everything seemed to get darker and Paimon started to feel dizzy... There were ghostly flames flickering all around, and...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon saw some sort of black mist surrounding the ghost, and then... Paimon passed out.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Hmm. Based on your account, it does really seem like you've seen a ghost.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! So, are you convinced it was a ghost now?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: It's possible, but I'm more interested in what she's actually trying to achieve than what she is.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Even if she is a ghost, as long as she possesses some sense of reason, then there must be some purpose behind her actions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wasn't she after our souls? She said that herself.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: I think she was just trying to scare you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? You think so?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Think about it: if I had the ability to take your souls, then why go to the trouble of warning you over and over again?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Besides, a ghost wouldn't have allowed you to walk away knowing about the secret of its powers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, that does make sense. Huh, why didn't Paimon think of that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Because you were always too scared to think straight.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: I believe there are only two possibilities. The first is that she wanted to reap your souls, but there was some condition that had to be met... You know, like what we usually call a curse.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: But if you had really been cursed, then you would probably have noticed it by now.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: So, this is the less likely scenario. I believe she was just trying to scare you away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But why would she want to scare us away...? Oh, Paimon knows!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe she was trying to get us to quit so she could claim the Test of Courage prizes!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Was she registered as a contestant?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, hmm probably not... So why does she want to scare us? Do you have any ideas, Heizou?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Based solely on your account, I don't believe she actually meant any harm. She just didn't want you to stay here.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: But this evidence alone is insufficient to make any valid assumptions. She could very well be guarding some treasure or covering up a crime.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Though... My intuition is telling me that neither of these hypotheses are correct. Let's continue investigating the surrounding area.

talks.objective: Look for clues in the area

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I've looked all around, but I haven't found any clues.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Looking up, there are a few branches that have been bent slightly downward, as if something heavy had been hanging from them.)

talks.objective: Look for clues in the area

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (There are some footprints visible on the ground.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (However, upon closer inspection, they seem to belong to Heizou and myself. Huh, could that woman really be a ghost...?)

talks.objective: Discuss what you just found with Heizou

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Have you found any leads yet?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I noticed some branches that seemed a little unusual.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, some tree branches seem like they were bent by something, but that's about it.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: I see. After you left, I took a good look around the area.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Aside from the bent branches, there are burn marks in some places, but that doesn't really tell us much.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: If only there was some more conclusive evidence...

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: Excuse me, uh... sorry to interrupt.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you guys! What are you all doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: We heard you were out searching for clues, and we wanted to help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, that's really brave of you!

dialogues.speaker: Kappa
dialogues.text: Uh, actually, we're also really unsure about what's happening here...

dialogues.speaker: Kappa
dialogues.text: We just asked the members of Mr. Itto's gang about what happened to them, and it sounded really scary.

dialogues.speaker: Kappa
dialogues.text: That lady is either a nasty evil spirit or a formidable youkai... Either way, it's not good.

dialogues.speaker: Kappa
dialogues.text: B—But we still want to hold the Mikawa Flower Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: Uh-huh!

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: We long admired the friendship between Lord Kamai and the Samurai.

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: Which is why we want to hold the Mikawa Flower Festival, to return the favor we once received from the humans.

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: Even though our powers are limited, we don't want this bond of friendship to vanish. The Mikawa Flower Festival is meant to be enjoyable for everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: The Chinju Forest covers a large area, so it'd be great to have more help in the investigation.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Welcome to the team. Let's all do our best to figure out what's going on.

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we're very familiar with the area. We won't miss any clues!

dialogues.speaker: Kappa
dialogues.text: *panting* ...

dialogues.speaker: Kappa
dialogues.text: Look what I found down by the river...

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: Oh? What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: Is it a scrap of black cloth? I've never seen fabric like this before.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Ah, this is a piece of shade cloth.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Shade cloth?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Yeah. It can effectively block out light and is used in a variety of settings, including stage performances.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: There is a rough tear in the cloth, probably caused by a sharp stone or maybe some branches...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Branches...?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Suppose that a large shade cloth was originally hung from a tree, bending the branches.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: When the shade cloth was removed from the tree, perhaps one of the corners caught and the branches ripped it, causing a small piece of black cloth to fall into the river.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Either she didn't care, or she was in too great a hurry. Perhaps she had other things to handle at the time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But why would she hang shade cloth in the trees?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: I'm only speculating, but...

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Maybe she used it to "create" the atmosphere you experienced.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Let's not worry about that for now. There are still many variables I haven't deduced yet.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Next, I'd like to investigate the place where the Arataki Gang encountered her. Do you know how to get there?

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: Oh, I know the way.

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: I asked the gang members where their encounter with the ghost happened when we were chatting earlier. I'll take you there!

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Good, please lead the way.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Let's go find out what's going on.

talks.objective: Follow the little youkai to the next investigation area

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: This is the place!

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: They claimed that as they passed through here, the area suddenly grew dark and some ghostly flames appeared out of nowhere...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, what a coincidence...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We saw the very same thing.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Let's start by taking a look around the area, just as we did before.

talks.objective: Look for clues in the area

dialogues.speaker: Kappa
dialogues.text: There's some strange powder in the cracks of these stones...

dialogues.speaker: Kappa
dialogues.text: I picked some up and sniffed it to see what it is, and it made me really dizzy... ugh, I'm so tired now...

talks.objective: Look for clues in the area

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: I found some sort of smashed ball under the tree.

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: The inside of it looks like it was blackened by smoke and it smells like fireworks.

talks.objective: Look for clues in the area

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: Judging from the burn marks left on the scene, the ghostly flames you saw were not created by youkai power.

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: Rather, they appear to have been caused by something flammable. I'm not sure what though...

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Hmm, similar scare tactics... and she didn't have the time to completely hide the traces...

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: I believe we're closing in on the truth now.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: I'm almost certain that the woman you encountered was not a ghost.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: She possesses no extraordinary powers. She was merely scaring people with some small props she had set up ahead of time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Some small props? But can you really do all that with just some props? What we saw was absolutely terrifying.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: First and foremost, the Test of Courage contributed to the unsettling atmosphere here.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: You were initially frightened by your first encounter with these three youkai, and then shortly after, you ran into the mysterious woman. It was natural for you to be on edge.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Because you were already tensed up, you were breathing more rapidly and inhaled a lot of sleeping powder that she had sprinkled around the area. That is what caused you to feel dizzy.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: That's when she pulled down the shade cloth and lit those so-called "ghostly flames," creating a terrifying scene... Hmm, that's the most likely explanation, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: So it was all just a show?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, she tricked us!

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: There is, however, still one loose end. The person who commissioned my investigation did become stranded on the beach as a result of some unusual power.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: That couldn't have been accomplished by just a few small props... But if she possesses such powers, why bother with the theatrics?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon can't wrap her head around all this.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: She can only use props to scare people in the forest, but she can use strange powers on the beach... I see. I think I've figured it out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah, that was fast!

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: If we rule out the potential of organized crime, then only one possibility remains.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: I know who the woman is. Let's go to the beach.

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: We'll come along, too!

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: No, you should go back and tell the others not to be afraid and not waste their time searching the forest.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: The truth has surfaced. It's time to put an end to all the unnecessary panic and await the outcome of the Test of Courage.

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: Okay, but please be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: If you run into any danger, simply call out our names. We'll be able to hear you.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: There shouldn't be any danger now, but thank you anyway. Let's go.

talks.objective: Look for anything unusual on the beach

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Hey, whatcha tryin' to say? Besides, it won't just be me! Other people will help too. Even my bro Ayato is gonna be there!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Everyone's busy getting ready, and the festival will be up and running in no time. It won't be long until you can all join the fun! Hahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Youko & Kappa & Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: You're the best, Itto!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: And what would a festival be without me? I'll be sure to go have a look, too.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Ah, it has been some time since I've attended a festival... Fortunately, I brought sake with me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's gotta admit, Itto does have his moments!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A festival, delicious food... Count Paimon in!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you want to join us, Chizuru?

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll join... If you don't mind, that is...
I knew it... I knew that you would come find me here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There she is!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thought you were a youkai like the others, but they said they'd never seen you before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So who are you? And why did you try to scare us?
I've already warned you never to speak to me. If you don't leave now, then...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek! She's terrifying! Heizou, it sure doesn't seem like she's using any props this time!

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Don't move! Just trust me.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Your youkai power won't scare us. It will only hasten your demise.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Youkai power?
Huh, how did you know?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: You're a youkai that emerged from an object and assumed a human form outside of your own body...

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: When this type of youkai is close to its own body, it can use some youkai power, but that ability weakens as it moves further away.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: And if the original body is destroyed, then the youkai that originated from it will likewise perish.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Should I refer to you as a "Hagoita Spirit" or "Tsukumogami"?

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: ...Don't bother. You may call me Hanyuuda Chizuru, that is the name I go by now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chizuru... why do you want us to leave?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you're a youkai, you should understand why the other youkai want to interact with humans...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Besides, we had a great time playing Akitsu Yuugei together, didn't we? Just like the story of Kamai and the samurai...

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Yes... that's why...

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: That's why I don't want you to be sad too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sad? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: I'm sure the youkai have already told you of the story about Kamai befriending the samurai.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: But they don't actually know the entire story.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Their friendship started as something they looked forward to, and in just a few decades, it turned into regret.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Lord Kamai's appearance hadn't changed, but his dear friend in front of him had grown old. The joys of friendship gradually gave way to the pain of regret.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: People often say that those outside the situation can see things more clearly, and I learned a harsh truth after witnessing all of it. Everything that people come to regret is inevitably set in motion from the beginning...

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: We youkai are different from humans, we have longer lifespans and different natures... But we share the same world, we interact with one another, we are drawn to one another, and will eventually part ways.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: When the dream ends, all that is left are sorrowful memories and lingering pain...

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Even a wise and seasoned youkai like Kamai felt sadness when it was time to say goodbye. Imagine what a pure and kind little youkai would feel.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, you mean...

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: I was hiding on this beach, waiting for the last of my days.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: But those three youkai came and set up the Akitsu Yuugei here, which woke me from my slumber.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: I didn't want them to approach humans with unbridled optimism and enthusiasm just because they'd heard the legend of Kamai and the samurai. That would simply be repeating the same mistake...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that why you pretended to be a ghost? To scare all the people away from here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... so you must be the one who trapped that guy on the beach? That was a little bit harsh, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: My power has become pretty weak now, and most of the time I just use some props I've collected to scare people. I can't show myself when there are a lot of people around.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: But that jerk was greedy. He wanted to steal the decorations from Akitsu Yuugei and sell them for a profit.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: That's why I used my youkai power to teach him a lesson.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, so that's what happened. You have a strong sense of justice.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the way, how did you know the rest of the story about Kamai and the samurai?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: It's okay if you don't want to tell us. I've already figured it out.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Your true form is this pair of hagoita, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hagoita? Ah, wait, so that means she's...

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: The pair of hagoita used by Kamai and the human samurai to play Akitsu Haz{RUBY#[S]Haneasobi}ura hundreds of years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: You gradually developed sentience after being influenced by great youkai power. You were the closest to witness their story.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Even with the youkai power's blessing, the hagoita have started to rot away after hundreds of years. You can't sustain yourself, so you were forced to rely on props to scare people.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: And, if my theory is correct, this pair of hagoita is also the item we need to find for the third round of the Test of Courage...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Excellent work. You've figured it all out.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Congratulations, little ones. You've passed the third round of the Test of Courage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Miko! And... the shrine maiden? Paimon thought you went missing.

dialogues.speaker: Shrine Maiden
dialogues.text: I apologize for causing you concern. It was actually Lady Yae's idea...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Haha, well? What did you think? Were you scared?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Because fear is induced by uncertainty, the more chaotic the situation, the better. Having the event staff also mysteriously vanish only added to the uncertainty... I must say, I think this Test of Courage truly lived up to its name.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you're the one responsible for all the scary stuff!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hitomi, go tell the others that the Test of Courage has ended and that we have a winner.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Now that I've solved the mystery, I'm going back to meet with my client. The "intent to steal" is not exactly a serious crime, but it can't go unpunished.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: I'll see you two later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Miko, did you choose the hagoita for the third round of the Test of Courage because you already knew about Chizuru?

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: "Miko"... "Lady Yae"... You're...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: I followed Kitsune Saiguu around the Mikawa Flower Festival one year and saw her play Akitsu Haz{RUBY#[S]Haneasobi}ura.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: That was when I saw you. You didn't have a human form at the time, and possessed only the earliest traces of sentience.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: I remember now, you were on Kitsune Saiguu's shoulder...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: I went for a stroll on the beach some time ago and sensed a familiar youkai power.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Though your power was weak, I was still able to find you. You were sitting in a tree, gazing at the tourists below.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: I overheard you telling yourself that you must be patient and avoid contact with humans.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Huh, when was that? I didn't notice you at all.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: With your powers being so diminished, it was only natural that you didn't notice me.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: You must have been blaming yourself all this time. You knew Kamai and the samurai became friends as a result of Akitsu Haz{RUBY#[S]Haneasobi}ura, a game connected to your existence.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: At the time, I couldn't take on a human form like this. I had only a hazy sense of the outer world.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: After they first met at the Mikawa Flower Festival, I felt proud to know that I had left a mark on their story.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: But after they said their final goodbyes, I could often hear Kamai sighing to himself. I couldn't help but hide, because I blamed myself. When I woke up again, the world had changed.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Lady Yae, you are a well-known youkai. You must know many more things than I do... so, I have a question for you...

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: People meet, become friends, and then go their separate ways. After such a short time, they leave only regret and sadness in their wake.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Is it really worthwhile for us youkai to interact with humans?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: #Why not? Tell me, how did you feel when you played Akitsu Yuugei with {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: I felt happy, but...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: But your "rationality" told you that it was wrong, didn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: It turns out that there is still another piece to the story of Kamai and the samurai that you are missing.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: What do you mean? The samurai and Kamai never met again.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: True, but the story doesn't end there. That samurai's name was Yanagibashi Takuto, who also happens to be the founder of the Souran Isshin Art.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: "It is believed that Takuto developed this style of swordsmanship while dueling with Kamai, who had also befriended the third-generation heir of the Souran Isshin Art, Tominaga Masanari."

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Five hundred years ago, Kamai and Tominaga fought side by side until their final moments, and the sword Tominaga wielded was passed down from Yanagibashi. The regret Kamai once felt had finally been resolved.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Oh... I never knew...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: We youkai are not like humans. Humans have too short a lifespan, and the day will inevitably come we when must say goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: However, the bond formed by friendship will not be broken, but rather, carried on in a new form.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: There's no reason to be upset by this. Time flies by in an instant, and life passes by like a dream. So, you must be happy in the present. You should understand what I mean now.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Hey, compadres!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Itto! What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Haha, Hitomi told me everything... and I also heard that you won the last round!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: I even know who the ghost lady is now. Anyway, I had a little discussion with the others and uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Hey, you're that fox lady! Why are you here?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hehe, please just disregard my presence. Now, tell us what you discussed.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Ah right, ahem! Alright, listen up! To celebrate the end of the Test of Courage event, we will be holding the Mikawa Flower Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: I gave it some real thought, and realized that it might be kinda difficult for those little youkai to hold the festival on their own. But with my help, it won't be a problem!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: That's right, Arataki "The One and Oni" Itto, will be in charge of organizing the best Mikawa Flower Festival anyone's ever seen!

dialogues.speaker: Youko & Kappa & Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: Hurray for Itto!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Oh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, can we really trust this guy with a festival?

talks.objective: Look for anything unusual on the beach

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Alright, here will do. Thank you for agreeing to come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't mention it.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Actually, I was delighted when I first discovered that I could take on a human form.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: I was a youkai derived from a pair of hagoita who came into being in the middle of a festival, so naturally I enjoyed the lively festival atmosphere.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: I wanted to go to more festivals, become friends with humans, and play Akitsu Yuugei with them.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: But every evening as night began to set in, I'd recall the bitter smile of the old samurai as he set down the hagoita, and the lonely Kamai sighing as he drank his sake.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Then I would wonder... if I became friends with a human, would that person experience the same melancholy in the future?

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: As a result, I was convinced that I couldn't do it. I told myself that I would not repeat that same mistake.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I understand what you mean.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: I'm sorry that I spoke so strangely when we first met... I'm sure it must have scared you.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: I expected you to flee in terror, but when we met again, you acted like you had no trouble being around me.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: I knew you mistook me as one of the youkai, but instead of telling you the truth, I went and played Akitsu Yuugei with you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why?

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Hmm... I'm not completely sure myself.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Perhaps it's because I've always wanted to be like Kamai and play Akitsu Yuugei with humans.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Or perhaps it was because I knew I didn't have much time left and I didn't want to be alone...

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Anyway, thank you for taking the time to play with me.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: When we played Akitsu Yuugei, Paimon said the loser would have to grant the winner a wish.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: At the time, I wished for us to never cross paths again.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: However, you still came and found me, meaning you never granted my wish. So... can I make another wish?

response.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
response.text: Let me think... I wish for you to remember me... Ah no, I only have one wish, so I'd better make it count.

response.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
response.text: Okay, listen carefully. My wish is...

response.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
response.text: "I wish that every day of your journey ahead will be filled with joy like a festival."

choices.text: As long as I can fulfill it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Itto! And Gorou! What are you two talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Oh, I was just saying that if I had more time, I'd have built a massive fishing pond here!

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Fishing... You know, when I lived on Watatsumi Island, I used to just dive into the sea and catch fish with my bare hands.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Haha! Take it from an expert, using your hands to catch fish is nowhere near as fun as using a fishing rod!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Just the other day I caught a fish so big that I didn't even know how to handle it... I even wrote a letter to Yae Publishing House about it.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: That's an unusual problem to have...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? A big fish? How come you didn't tell us? Paimon could have helped you eat it!

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Huh? You wrote a letter to Yae Publishing House?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: You bet I did! I wrote to the "That's Life" column and asked Miss Hina for advice. She's so amazing, she got back to me really quickly, too!

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Huh, what a coincidence. I do some part-time work there, and I recently received a similar letter.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: You mean the letter was about dealing with a giant fish they caught? No... could it be...

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Could it be that there's someone as good at fishing as I am? Not on my watch... Hey, you all go enjoy the festival, I'm gonna get out there and catch an even bigger fish!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Just you wait, I'll be inviting you all to my fish feast! Hahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: Ah, the string snapped! I was so close!

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: Yoimiya, this is more difficult than it looks. Can you really fish out these water balloons with a string?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Don't worry. Let me show you a little trick. Just remember that your hand has to be quick!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yo-yo Tsuri! Paimon's seen this game in some light novels before!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Do you want to give it a shot? Close one eye, aim carefully, and fish it out quickly!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh, it looks kinda tricky. Paimon will let {NICKNAME} try. You have to catch at least three water balloons since there's three of us.

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: Uh, but Yoimiya, if I close one eye, I won't be able to see anything!

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Mmm, this ramen is so good...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Yes, it feels like it's been ages since the last time I had some.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? You mean you don't get to eat ramen very often, Ayaka? But it's so delicious!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you. We'll need two more bowls of ramen, please.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Food like ramen and hotpot tend to have a lot of oil and salt, so I don't get to eat them very often.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Oh, that's unfortunate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, now Paimon totally gets why Ayaka would put cake into hotpot.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... please, no need to bring that up again...

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Whew, I'm stuffed... and feeling a little sleepy. I'm just gonna... take a nap...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: By the way, were there any special stalls at youkai festivals in the past?

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Yes, but... Well, it's a long story.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can't believe you couldn't get a single water balloon. You've gotten rusty!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chizuru managed to finally get one and gave it to Hitotsume Kozou...

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: He looked like he really wanted it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon wanted one, too!

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Alright, then I'll catch one for you next time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay!

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: C'mon now, this is way more expensive than usual! Even if it is a festival, you shouldn't hike up the prices this much.

dialogues.speaker: Tomohiro
dialogues.text: Hey now, it costs money to run a stall! I need to raise my prices to help cover the expenses, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Fair enough, how about five masks for 30% off? Final offer.

dialogues.speaker: Tomohiro
dialogues.text: Alright, alright...

dialogues.speaker: Kappa
dialogues.text: Ah, it's so hot. Feels like I'm being roasted here!

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Don't get too close, it's better to keep a few steps back.

dialogues.speaker: Kappa
dialogues.text: I know... It's just so rare to see such a nice bonfire! I want to get as close as I can to enjoy it.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: There are many beautiful things in the world, there's no need to be anxious. The festival has only just begun...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: I was surprised that you didn't even tell your sister. It seems she was quite frightened, too.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: It would have been uninteresting had I told her what was going to happen ahead of time.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Besides, with her friends by her side, she wouldn't ever be too scared. Having a little fright is good to release any tension she might have accumulated lately.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hehe, everything went according to plan. People started to panic as soon as they sensed that they had no idea what was happening. Ah, how amusing.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Hehe... Yes, well done.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you two! Stop laughing! It was scary!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hmm? Have you finished exploring the festival?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just about.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Well then, are you having a good time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! It's great!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: The original Mikawa Flower Festival was much more lively. But even if you could attend the original, you probably wouldn't be as happy as you are now.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Because it's always more fun to enjoy a festival with friends, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: ...Yes. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: #Well then, I'm guessing you have something you want to say to {M#him}{F#her} alone? We'll leave you in peace.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? What did you want to say to us?

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: Ah, you saw through me again... I can't help but feel you somehow know everything.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: It's not that I "know everything." It's just that I've been in your position before.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, do you have a moment? I'd like to talk to you... alone on the beach.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: When Ayato approached me about holding the Test of Courage event, it dawned on me that this would be the perfect opportunity to help Chizuru face her problem.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Kamai and the samurai's parting was one of the first things she experienced when she was partially sentient and didn't have her human form yet.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: This was a very traumatic experience for her, and she could never come to grips with it by reasoning alone.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: The best option was for her to directly interact with humans. There's no need to feel sad, I believe she was content when she left us.

talks.objective: Meet Hanyuuda Chizuru at the beach

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: It was heartbreaking to learn of Chizuru's story.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: To be honest, I experience that same kind of sorrow when I'm on the battlefield. I don't know when I'll lose my comrades, so I try to appreciate every moment.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: It's not that I "know everything." It's just that I've been in your position before.

dialogues.speaker: Hanyuuda Chizuru
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, do you have a moment? I'd like to talk to you... alone on the beach.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Every year, when the fireworks go off, I say to myself, "Another year has already passed."

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: As each year passes by, your life gradually approaches its end.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: But I don't think that's a bad thing. Like I always say, fireworks are for now, but friends are forever.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Lifespans, partings... It really gets you thinking, doesn't it? ...But uh, I got nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Alls I know is that I'll never regret meeting you! Hahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: So, did you enjoy the Test of Courage?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Once I learned of the youkai's intentions to hold a festival, I wanted to spread the word and attract people to their event.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: However, it occurred to me that doing so might be overly ambitious. If we marketed the Mikawa Flower Festival from the get-go, people would have arrived with insatiably high expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: So I decided on using the Test of Courage's notoriety to attract visitors and left the rest to the youkai.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I had an inkling that their presence would spice up the event, hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Ah, after hearing Chizuru describe the original Mikawa Flower Festival, I wanted to arrange another chance to talk with her about it.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I didn't expect that would be our last conversation...

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Will you have some time in the next few days, Kazuha?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: I'd like you to work on a case with me.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Oh? Did you run into some trouble?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Not exactly. It's just an old case with almost no tangible leads.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: But I believe your attuned sense of nature might allow us to discover some new clues.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Sure. I can stay after the festival and we can go investigate together.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Great, thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: My pleasure. It's no trouble at all.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Even though I knew my lord had most likely planned everything before the Test of Courage even began, I was still caught off guard.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: But, in retrospect, it was a lot of fun.

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Zzz... I've grown taller... hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: I'm so tall... Everyone else looks so tiny now... Zzz...

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Weird... Where did all the fish go?

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Don't worry. Let's go try another spot.

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: Aww no... I almost had it!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Starting to get the hang of it, huh? Keep trying!

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Zzz...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: One bowl of ramen shouldn't hurt, right?...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: I sure bought a lot of stuff... I'll have to organize it all when I get back.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Are you enjoying yourself? How about we go eat together?

dialogues.speaker: Kappa
dialogues.text: I think I need to take a break...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Saying goodbye is also part of a festival.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: ...Yes, every celebration must come to an end.

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: I want to become a great youkai, like the mighty Urakusai...

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: Then I'll be able to help create a real Mikawa Flower Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Aha...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've been waiting quite a while, but the shrine maiden still hasn't shown up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like we'll just have to start the third round without her. Who will we team up with this time?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Let's search along the cliffside. If I'm not mistaken, there should be a chunk of earth that's unlike the others...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like the festival has started! Let's go check it out!
